correctness.rationale: The twelve rational Cartesian vertices imply eighteen equal-angle edges. An exhaustive six-cell normal partition with exact vertex-sign boundaries proves N in {4,5,6}. Two spherical triangle angles yield P6, while the independent Crofton-type edge separation identity gives E[N], determining P4 and P5. The embedded checker verifies rational sign cells, all spherical cell areas, radical denominators, normalization, and a rational strict pentagonal-majority certificate. No finite test substitutes for the exact proof.

value.rationale: The full probability law for central polygonal sections of a natural Archimedean polyhedron is a motivated, nontrivial finite classification. It demonstrates three possible section types, exact spherical angular weights, and a predominant pentagonal type. The combinatorial sign arrangement and two nontrivial radical arctangents are not routine restatements of cube-section probabilities.
